standard.title: Mapping and location
standard.description: interpret and create two-dimensional representations of familiar environments, locating key landmarks and objects relative to each other
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate positions in two-dimensional representations of a familiar space and move positions by following directions and pathways (AC9M2SP02). They have not yet created their own two-dimensional maps or described the relative positions of multiple landmarks simultaneously.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret and create two-dimensional maps of familiar environments, locating landmarks and objects relative to each other.

nodes.label: Interpreting 2D maps
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a 2D map to locate key landmarks and describe their positions relative to each other using directional and spatial language.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a given 2D map to locate three landmarks and describe the position of two relative to a third using spatial language.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret a range of 2D maps (classroom, school grounds, local area); locate landmarks and describe relative positions using compass directions, grid references and spatial language.
wider: Interpret aerial photographs and compare them with drawn maps — exploring what information each representation emphasises
Explore how First Nations Australians represent country in maps, artworks and stories, comparing with Western mapping conventions

response_modes.reason: Students often interpret maps of only one type (school grounds) and cannot transfer spatial reasoning to other contexts. Encountering varied representations — including aerial photos and First Nations maps — broadens the concept of what a map is.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations mapping traditions and the comparison with aerial photography provide genuine conceptual richness about representation, perspective and the social purposes of mapping.
success_criteria: Students can locate a specified landmark on a 2D map.
Students can describe the position of one landmark relative to another using spatial language.

nodes.label: Creating 2D maps
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create a 2D representation of a familiar environment that shows the key landmarks and their relative positions.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a simple map of a familiar space (e.g. classroom or bedroom) showing at least four landmarks in approximately correct relative positions.
nodes.typical_width: Create 2D maps of familiar environments with an appropriate key, scale indication and correct relative positions of landmarks; evaluate maps against the actual environment.
wider: Create maps of the school grounds or local area using grid references, comparing the map with a digital satellite view
Use digital mapping tools to create and annotate maps, discussing the conventions used by digital platforms
success_criteria: Students can create a 2D map of a familiar space with landmarks placed in approximately correct relative positions.
Students can explain why they placed a landmark where they did in relation to another landmark.
